dek: A proposed synthetic-data exercise checks whether agent traces expose failures and support repeatable evaluation.

stories.title: A proposed trace test checks agent failures and hidden data
stories.summary: Editorialge proposes testing observability tools with the same synthetic workflow, including a failed tool call and an incorrect answer.
body: Agent observability tools record the steps between a request and an answer. Editorialge’s comparison proposes a practical exercise for checking whether that record actually supports investigation. A trace can help explain execution, but it does not establish that an answer is correct or a customer’s task is complete.

First, the guide suggests using synthetic data in one representative workflow: retrieve a policy, call a test interface, and summarize the result. Check whether the model request, retrieval, and tool operation appear as connected steps. Then deliberately fail the tool operation and inspect whether its error and duration are visible without exposing credentials.

Next, check that reviewers can identify the prompt, model, and application used. Capture an incorrect answer that appeared to succeed and see whether it can become a repeatable evaluation. Finally, inspect retained data, access permissions, and expected volume costs. This is a proposed test plan, with no measured comparison results.
stories.takeaway: Teams comparing trace tools can use a shared synthetic failure case to check coverage before expanding instrumentation.

image_provenance.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: standalone PNG newspaper story infographic.
Primary request: illustrate Editorialge’s proposed synthetic-data test for agent observability. Source: https://editorialge.com/ai-agent-observability-tools/ . This is a proposed exercise, not measured results or a product screenshot. Source-supported mechanism: run one synthetic workflow, deliberately fail a tool call, inspect recorded error and duration without credentials, capture an incorrect answer as a repeatable evaluation, check retained data and access.
Style: warm cream newsprint, dark ink line illustration, restrained rust-red accent, generous spacing, serif title, large readable labels. Landscape 3:2 composition, four connected illustrated elements with clean arrows. No logos or invented metrics.
Text verbatim, only these labels: Title "Test what the trace reveals"; subtitle "Proposed exercise • synthetic data"; four panels "Run a workflow", "Fail a tool call", "Inspect the evidence", "Check data access". Small annotation under panel three: "Error • duration • answer". Show a simple document and tool, a broken tool symbol, a magnifying glass on a trace record, and a locked data cabinet. All arrows left to right, no claim that tracing proves correctness. No footer, no watermark, no extra text.
